What's the safest way to download torrents.
Are you using a browser VPN? Because if so the torrents won't go through it when downloading, you need a client to server VPN.
How's a browser vpn different from a client to server vpn? How do i avoid getting caught while "swashbuckling on the high seas", so to speak?

An in-browser VPN only encrypts your traffic inside that particular browser, so once the torrent starts downloading in your torrent software (Deluge or whatever), it is no longer encrypted traffic. A client to server VPN changes your actual network adapter settings on your PC, encrypting ALL traffic coming out of your ethernet port and sending ALL of it to the VPN server first. Depending on the service they either give you software that you turn on and it does it for you, or you set up the VPN connection in your network adapter settings on your PC. I don't know of many reliable free ones though. I just use them for my work networks.

EDIT: For some more detail, in the browser, they might not be able to see what you're browsing, but once you start downloading, they can see the P2P connections coming in from everyone seeding you, and can tell whats going on. With a VPN, all they can see is one constant stream of encrypted traffic to one location, and since it's all encrypted they can't tell if you're watching porn, netflix, or stealing movies.

Your best bet is to get a VPN that also provides a socks5 proxy. You can then add this to your torrent client in your options in case your VPN switches off for a short while(exposing your real ip).
